Subjective items such as screen and system user experience are not taken into account.
prefaceThe annual bushi is just around the corner, and as we all know, Heyi Meigao's ban on the use of electronic devices on campus is basically nonsense after just a few months of school, allowing everything except mobile phones to be used freely. As we all know, because textbooks are as heavy as bricks, many students tend to use tablets to read electronic textbooks and take class notes. The current electronics market is a mixed bag, with all sorts of brands rushing to make tablets (specifically Lenovo Xiaoxin, whose tablets are pure electronic garbage). So today, Heyi Meigao Hardware Society brings you a guide to buying tablets at different price points and for different needs now and in the next six months. FaithThere's a kind of mental disability called Apple, a kind of patriotism called Huawei, and an explosion called Samsung (bushi). Judging from the names, everyone knows who I'm criticizing. The first two are the ones I think definitely need to be carefully considered. The reason is simple: the closed system ecosystem means that you can almost only buy the complete set, as well as the high price and low cost-effectiveness (the latter two are especially relevant to Apple). To give a simple example: Suppose Zhang San buys an iPad air5 (256GB), then in order to take notes, he also needs a second-generation Apple Pencil and an official Apple Magic Control keyboard. The total original price of these three items on JD.com is 8550 RMB, which is now enough for a high-end computer mainframe. Moreover, once you buy a tablet, you must buy an iPhone and an Apple computer to achieve the best ecosystem synergy and maximum efficiency (I can write a separate article about why later). The iPhone 13 Pro 256G version is priced at 8200 on JD.com, the M1 version of the MacBook Air 13 is 7400, and the M2 version is 9200. A complete set would cost at least two thousand yuan. Forgive my bluntness, whoever buys it is an idiot (just ignore the fact that my family is so poor they only have money left). Huawei's situation is similar, but in fact, Huawei's most important problem does not lie here, but in other aspects, which I will introduce in detail below. Apple EditionOnce you've made up your mind to put up with Apple's poor software compatibility and game isolation on your computer, please read on. Alternatively, you can choose to jump to the Huawei section. First, let me state my personal opinion: I won't buy pro unless it's necessary. The difference between the iPad air and iPad pro isn't that significant for the average consumer!ipad air Whether it's performance or user experience, it's hard to truly appreciate it without using an iPad for video editing. The same applies to gaming; the same M1 chip can completely handle the current performance killer, Genshin Impact. Taking notes goes without saying. To be honest, Apple really doesn't have much to say about it. It has a solid screen and stylus quality, a smooth system, and a whole host of other advantages. The only problem is its price. If you don't play games and won't need very specialized software for your college major in the future, but just want to use it for reading, writing, and taking notes, and your budget is not limited, then the Apple family bucket is indeed a good choice. Finally, when buying Apple products, please remember: Buy what you need, don't create demand. Beware of Cook's knife technique [doge] Huawei EditionActually, I didn't originally want to include Huawei in the discussion, but since many people only know about Huawei besides Apple, I'll bring it up anyway. One thing is clear: HarmonyOS is not a user-friendly "mobile phone" system; its real advantage lies in the Internet of Everything. Never buy Huawei just because of HarmonyOS; its advantages may not be apparent for the next five years. Moreover, the desktop mode of the HarmonyOS system (the mode in which tablets improve the mouse and keyboard user experience by imitating the computer interface) is very poorly designed, almost unusable. Then comes a common misconception: the so-called "support for domestic products". Huawei has never been a conscientious company. Admittedly, Huawei is awesome, truly awesome. It is one of only four mobile phone manufacturers in the world that can design its own chips, and it has also modified Android to develop its own HarmonyOS system. However, it's really not as good as most people imagine. The Enjoy series is a huge rip-off for the poor, with the best configuration in the same price range coupled with the highest price. After being sanctioned, prices skyrocketed, with the P50E 778G chip selling for 4,000 yuan (compared to 2,000 yuan for the same Xiaomi configuration). Back when Huawei was still using Android 10's EMUI, it blatantly violated Google's Android Open Source Convention by blocking bl and root channels. (If anyone criticizes me for worshipping foreign things, please take a look up. I also criticize Apple, much harsher than Huawei.) In short, Huawei is indeed facing difficulties, but its current products offer very low cost-effectiveness. As consumers, especially those with limited budgets, the primary consideration should be whether their products are worth their investment, rather than whether they support so-called national enterprises and patriotism. Next, we'll begin the official Huawei tablet recommendation. If you only want to do light office work and study, the MatePad 11 (3999 + 600 + 450) is a good option.matepad11 If you want to play some games, you'll need Pro 2021 (3299 + 600 + 450).matepad pro Samsung EditionSamsung's newly released tab s8 series tablets this year (s8 4500-5700+700, s8+ 5700-7000+700, s8 ultra 7900-8900+700) call themselves the "King of Android Tablets." Although I still have doubts about whether this lousy 8-for-1 chip can be worthy of the King of Tablets, it must be said that Samsung is currently the most powerful manufacturer deeply involved in styluses. Samsung's first stylus was the one that came with the note1 11 years ago. Eleven years have passed since then, and its technological accumulation is not something that other manufacturers can easily catch up with. Based on my own experience, I believe that Samsung's note-taking experience is on par with Apple's and slightly surpasses Apple's. One of Samsung's notable features is its DEX mode. Samsung does a pretty good job with this computer mode. Personally, I was forced to use a tablet to work because my computer broke down, but now I haven't turned it on for two months. In terms of performance, the new generation Snapdragon 8 is quite good, but it gets very hot... (I personally tested it; this article was typed using a Samsung tab s8 with an external mechanical keyboard.) Samsung tab s8The looks are alright too (in my personal opinion). Finally, a purchase recommendation: The difference between the s8 series products is almost only in screen size. The stylus of the s8+/ultra has a very slight improvement over the s8 (6ms-2.8ms). Because it's a near-native system, it can be paired with any Android phone (though the user experience isn't very good either). If you have a limited budget, you can buy the base model s8 (which I am currently using), but based on my own experience, I recommend the s8+. Meanwhile, there are reports that Samsung is about to launch the s8FE, which will use the Snapdragon 8+Gen1 chip. If you can afford to wait, you should definitely wait! The difference between these two chips is stark. Summary of the products in the Faith section above: Choose wisely and avoid falling into traps, but the price is not worthwhile, and it is worth considering if you have a very sufficient budget. Cost-effectivenessHaving discussed high-end tablets, let's move on to the mid-to-low-end market. Unlike the hidden struggle in the high-end market, the mid-to-low-end market is truly "like water and fire". Xiaomi, OPPO, VIVO, Honor, as well as Apple's digital series and Huawei's low-end series are fiercely competing here. Next, we will introduce them one by one. Xiaomi EditionThe top contender is the Xiaomi Mi Tablet 5/5 pro (1999~2499 +350+400). As a tablet with a stylus latency of 22ms (Samsung's industry-leading 2.8ms, most others are between 6-9ms, and the sensation is generally not noticeable below 10ms), it can be ruled out as a learning tablet. At the same time, MIUI for pad cannot be said to be particularly good. Although the performance of the Xiaolong 860/870 combined with its price provides an excellent daily entertainment and gaming experience, the most important use of tablets in this article is for learning. Therefore, the Xiaomi pad 5 is not recommended for purchase.Xiaomi Tablet 5 However, there are reports that the Xiaomi Mi Pad 6 has effectively improved the above problems. Patient students can wait until the first half of the year, as it might be a very cost-effective option. OPPOThe second contender is OPPO's first tablet, the OPPO pad (2200~3000 +350+500). As the first tablet from a green factory, OPPO has shown great sincerity. Whether it is the 2k high refresh rate, the large battery or the LCD eye-protecting screen, it is basically on par with other mainstream tablet manufacturers. Although the stylus latency reached 16ms due to lack of experience, and the keyboard is not magnetically charged but has a built-in battery, resulting in an overall thickness, considering its price... it's not impossible to use. If you are currently using a new OPPO phone released in the last two years, then the OPPO pad can be considered one of your high-quality choices. OPPO pad However, please note: OPPO also has another, even lower-priced OPPO pad air. In my opinion, it's pure electronic garbage. It can only play iQiyi and games, so it's not included in the recommended list. vivoThe third place winner is the vivo pad (2500~3000 +350+600). The blue manufacturer followed the green manufacturer into the pad market this year, but its performance can only be described as less than satisfactory. Although its basic specifications and price are roughly the same as the O-board, it falls short in terms of the stylus, which most affects the learning experience, with a latency of 17.5ms. non-magnetic chargingTherefore, its stylus is relatively heavier and thicker. The fact that I need to replace the battery myself makes me list it and the Xiaomi tablet's stylus as unusable, so overall I don't recommend buying it. vivo pad Apple's low-end versionThe fourth place goes to a heavyweight player: the iPad 2021, also known as the iPad 9 (2500~3700 +730). As a player in Apple's digital series, which focuses on the low-end market, I have to say it's very tempting. Its powerful processor and screen, which are almost identical to the air Pro, make it an excellent tablet for "audio-visual entertainment". iPad 9 Attentive students should have noticed that I didn't mention its learning experience. That's right, the learning experience on this tablet can't be described as good; it's practically unusable. First, it doesn't have an official magnetic keyboard; you can only choose to use an external third-party keyboard or type on the screen, which directly eliminates productivity queues.Secondly, it uses the first-generation iPad pencil, which cannot magnetically charge, and its charging method is bizarre, comparable to an Apple mouse, resulting in poor latency (due to Apple's manipulation, I couldn't find the latency parameters for the high-end Apple pencil 1, but according to reviews, it should be around 20ms).Finally, it's really ugly (personal opinion, light criticism). Huawei Low-EndThe fifth contestant is arguably in the same heavyweight class as the Apple I just took away: the Huawei M6 tablet (1600~2300 +0). Why is the price +0? Because it does not support stylus, nor does it support the official magnetic keyboard. Isn't that outrageous? The mold is from three years ago, and the chip is from Kirin 980 inventory. This can sell for the same or even higher price as Xiaomi tablets. It has to be said that Huawei really has a knack for ripping off the poor. Huawei Tablet M6 My Samsung tab s3 from four or five years ago looks better than him. (Personal opinion, you can also find it beautiful) Similar to the V-board, Guozi low-end, and Mi5, it is classified as a non-recommended purchase. ##Glory EditionSixth place, and the last player in the low-to-mid-range category, is the Honor Tablet v7 Pro. Honor Tablet V7 Pro It must be said that the Honor tablet is deeply inherited from its father, Huawei. Although it bypasses sanctions, it does not affect the fact that the processor is extremely bad. Whether it is the MediaTek 1300T in the V7 Pro or the Snapdragon 680 in the Honor tablet 8, it can only be said to be limited to daily learning and light gaming. However, its stylus experience seems to be quite good. Although I have doubts about its 2ms advertising, it is definitely not much different, and it is still very good for taking notes. If you happen to own a recent Honor phone but don't play games much, then the Honor Tablet V7 Pro would be the perfect choice. Special Tablet EditionAlthough the tablet positioning of various companies generally follows the standards of mid-to-low-end and high-end product lines, there will always be a few exceptions. prefaceAs the matter escalated, on February 13, Lenovo's official Xiaoxin Weibo account responded to the incident with an article titled "Xiaoxin Light and Thin Notebook Low-Temperature Solder Paste Soldering Technology Description" (hereinafter referred to as the "Description"). The document stated that low-temperature solder paste soldering is a mature and more environmentally friendly technology for electronic product production lines that meets national and international standards. It also indicated that, based on after-sales data from Xiaoxin Light and Thin Notebooks over the years, there is no difference in repair rates between models using low-temperature solder paste soldering technology and models using room-temperature solder soldering technology. FirstI myself use a Lenovo Xiaoxin computer. I bought it from JD.com's self-operated flagship store in November last year (2022). The model is Xiaoxin 14 PRO-IAH5R, and the price is 6199 (I personally feel that this price is reasonable). My first impression of it is that it is light, too light. According to official data, the 14Pro weighs 1.3kg, roughly the same as the weight of the 2020 MacBook Air. Even with a 100W gallium nitride charger, its portability and thinness are beyond doubt. SecondlyRegarding this low-temperature tin incident, I do not believe it is part of Lenovo's planned scrapping. After watching the video of a laptop repair guy on Bilibili (I'm a fan of his), I found that most of the problems were with AMD platform machines. As is well known, AMD is notoriously hot, and some of the machines that undergo empty soldering are caused by high-temperature desoldering of on-board memory. This may be due to the unreasonable design of the heat dissipation structure at the time. Among the Intel models affected, I analyzed that it was because Lenovo used too much vinyl, which caused the CPU to be fixed. When the motherboard deformed due to the shaking of the computer, the CPU could not move, causing the solder ball to be misaligned. So this gives us a lesson:Don't shake your computer unless necessary. Be careful to hold it firmly.。 Therefore, I believe it is a design flaw. in the endWhat if it happens to you? My advice is to try not to contact Lenovo after-sales service. In the two months since I bought it, I've realized that Lenovo's after-sales service is exceptionally poor. I can say that some of the after-sales engineers' understanding of computers and their problem-solving methods are not even as good as some of my classmates. So, if you encounter this problem, it seems you can get it repaired for free under warranty (?). If it's out of warranty, go find a repair technician you're familiar with in a computer store. They might only charge a labor fee to resolder the unsoldered parts. Lenovo's after-sales service will directly replace the motherboard for you.I need 1000Then the price would be a bit high. In conclusion, I do not believe that the "low-temperature tin incident" was part of Lenovo's planned scrapping; it may simply be caused by a design flaw. Secondly, to avoid these problems as much as possible, you'd better hold on tight. Finally, if you get scammed, just go through the warranty and find a repairman to fix it. There's really no need to send it to official after-sales service (waves).

Review of the Honor Magic5 series The Honor Magic5 series is a flagship phone released by Honor on March 6, 2023, including two models: the Honor Magic5 and the Honor Magic5 Pro. Both phones are equipped with the new Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 processor, an OLED screen that supports a 120Hz refresh rate, and a rear camera with a three-body star ring design. So, what's the difference between them? Which one is more suitable for you? Let's compare them. First, in terms of appearance, both the Honor Magic5 and Magic5 Pro feature a quad-curved screen design, but the screen size and resolution differ. The Honor Magic5 has a 6.73-inch screen with a resolution of 2688×1224 pixels, while the Honor Magic5 Pro has a 6.81-inch screen with a resolution of 2848×1312 pixels. Both support 1.07 billion color displays and a wide DCI-P3 color gamut, but in terms of peak brightness, the Honor Magic5 Pro is higher, reaching 1800 nits, while the Honor Magic5 is 1600 nits. In addition, the Honor Magic5 Pro also supports LTPO technology, which can adaptively adjust the refresh rate according to the content, saving battery power while ensuring smoothness. Secondly, in terms of performance, the Honor Magic5 series all use the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 processor, which is an SoC chip based on the 4nm process, with powerful computing power, graphics processing capabilities and AI performance. Both are equipped with a combination of LPDDR5X memory and UFS 4.0 flash memory, and offer two storage capacity options: 256GB and 512GB. However, in terms of memory, the Honor Magic5 is only available in 8GB and 12GB specifications, while the Honor Magic5 Pro has a top-of-the-line version with 16GB. In addition, the Honor Magic5 Pro is exclusively equipped with a Display Chip that can assist the processor in tasks such as graphics rendering and video encoding and decoding. Secondly, in terms of photography, the Honor Magic5 series all adopts a three-body star ring design rear camera module and has the same configuration: a 50-megapixel wide-angle main camera + a 122° ultra-wide-angle lens + a high-definition macro lens. Regarding the front-facing camera, there are some differences: the Honor Magic5 uses a 42-megapixel single-camera solution, and both the internal and external screens are equipped with front-facing cameras; The Honor Magic5 Pro uses a 50-megapixel dual-camera design and only has a front-facing camera on the internal screen. entry.title: Honor Qinghai Lake & Solid-State Battery Technology | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Honor Magic5 series "Qinghai Lake" battery technologyThe Honor Magic5 is a highly anticipated smartphone that has recently sparked widespread discussion because it features a new battery technology known as "Qinghai Lake Battery Technology". Qinghai Lake is China's largest inland saltwater lake and one of the highest lakes in the world. Due to its high altitude, dry and cold climate, the lake water contains a large amount of beneficial elements such as lithium and magnesium. The Honor Magic5's battery technology utilizes these elements to improve battery performance and lifespan. Specifically, Qinghai Lake battery technology uses lithium-magnesium-silicon (LMS) material, a new type of battery material that has higher energy density and longer lifespan than traditional lithium-ion batteries. This material can not only increase battery capacity, but also improve the battery's fast charging capacity and stability, while reducing the battery's volume and weight. In addition, the Honor Magic5 also adopts intelligent temperature control technology, which can adjust the battery temperature in a timely manner during use to prevent overheating and overdischarge, thereby ensuring the safety and stability of the battery. The advantages of Qinghai Lake battery technology lie in its sustainability and environmental friendliness. The material resources of this technology come from nature and have the potential for recycling. In addition, this technology can reduce the impact of battery waste on the environment, which is beneficial to environmental protection and sustainable development. Overall, the Honor Magic5's Qinghai Lake battery technology is an exciting innovation that not only improves battery performance and lifespan, but also has environmental and sustainable advantages. It is believed that in the future, this new battery technology will be more widely used, bringing new opportunities for the development of smartphones and other electronic devices. Solid-state battery technology in mobile phonesWith the development of smartphones, battery life has become an increasingly important issue. To meet users' demand for long battery life, mobile phone manufacturers have been exploring new battery technologies. Among them, solid-state battery technology has attracted much attention. Solid-state battery technology is a new type of battery technology. Its main feature is that it uses solid electrolytes instead of traditional liquid electrolytes. Compared to traditional batteries, solid-state batteries have higher energy density, longer lifespan, and safer characteristics. At the same time, it can significantly reduce the volume and weight of the battery. Compared to traditional batteries, solid-state batteries have the following advantages:
Higher energy density. Solid-state batteries have a higher energy density than traditional batteries because they use more efficient materials and a tighter structure. Longer lifespan. Solid-state batteries are less prone to problems such as battery swelling and evaporation of liquid electrolytes, and therefore can maintain efficient and stable performance for a longer period of time. Safer. Because solid-state electrolytes are stable solids, solid-state batteries are safer under extreme conditions such as high temperatures, short circuits, overcharging, and overdischarging. Less volume and weight. Since solid-state batteries do not require liquid electrolytes and leak-proof structures, smaller and lighter batteries can be designed.
Solid-state battery technology has very broad application prospects, and can be used not only in smartphones, but also in other electronic devices and electric vehicles. Currently, some manufacturers have begun developing solid-state battery technology and have achieved some encouraging results in the laboratory. However, solid-state battery technology still faces some challenges, such as high manufacturing costs and difficult production. Therefore, a great deal of research and development is still needed in the future to enable this technology to be widely applied to the market.

Honor 90 series phone review: 200-megapixel main camera, 3840Hz high-frequency PWM dimming screen, combining thinness and battery life.The Honor 90 series is Honor's latest flagship phone, officially released on May 29, 2023. The 8-megapixel ultra-wide-angle camera supports a 123° ultra-wide-angle field of view, allowing you to capture a wider range of landscapes. The 2-megapixel macro camera supports 4cm close-up focus and can photograph subtle objects. The 2-megapixel macro camera and 2-megapixel depth-of-field camera are also the same as those in the Honor 90. image These parameters show that the Honor 90 Pro is more powerful than the Honor 90 in terms of camera, with better performance in both the main camera, telephoto lens, and ultra-wide-angle lens. If you are a user with high requirements for mobile phone photography, then the Honor 90 Pro is undoubtedly a better choice. Range and chargingThe Honor 90 and Honor 90 Pro also have different performances in terms of battery life and charging. entry.title: Xiaomi 13 Ultra Half-Year Usage Report - Xiaomi 13 Ultra Demystification | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. This article is a six-month usage report of Xiaomi's 2023 imaging flagship. It is an original work by Aden and may not be reproduced without permission.
In early 2024, when the Xiaomi 14 Ultra was released, I bought a reduced-price Xiaomi annual imaging flagship at an extremely low price. This phone was once rated as having the strongest imaging capabilities in 2023, and it is also Xiaomi's second Ultra camera after its collaboration with Leica.
This picture clearly shows the exaggerated image quality of this phone. Some people say that this phone is not a qualified phone, but more like a camera. I. AppearanceThe most impressive aspect of this phone's appearance is undoubtedly its fastback design. My impression after using this phone is that "it succeeds and fails." Why do I say that? Because without this sloping back, this phone probably wouldn't be able to fit four large-sensor optical lenses. The reason it's a sloping back is because this sloping back gives the phone a very poor grip. I usually use this phone with my index finger pressed against the lens, otherwise the phone would flip over due to headaches. Besides the fastback, what makes this 13 Ultra different from ordinary phones is that its back panel adopts a padded design, which means that vegetable leather is filled in the middle frame, which is a unique design language. This design was carried over to the 14Ultra. One advantage of this design approach is that the middle frame can be made very solid. During my daily bare-bones use, I could clearly feel that the mid-frame was integrated with the entire phone, giving it a very rugged feel. II. Image SectionAs a flagship imaging device, the focus of this phone should be on imaging. First, let's talk about the mainThe main camera is an IMX989 from Sony. This CMOS chip originally appeared on the Xiaomi 12 Sultra and was jointly developed by Xiaomi and Sony. Xiaomi monopolized the market for six months before Sony allowed other mobile phone manufacturers to use it. This CMOS chip is 1 inch in size, and theoretically it can perform very well in low-light environments. But in actual use, I can only say that a perfectly good 1-inch screen was ruined by Xiaomi's terrible night view algorithm. In areas with many light signs, 13Ultra won't apply highlighter; the light signs will directly expose you to white. Then, when encountering warm or white light, there's a chance the white balance will drift, resulting in photos that are stark white with a hint of gray. It cannot handle complex light sources and has severe glare. I used the default mode when taking this picture; I didn't apply a lens film, and the lens was wiped clean. It is said that the Xiaomi 14 Ultra has improved coating, which should have a better effect than the 13 Ultra. The 13Ultra's night scene algorithm scheduling is very passive. The default mode is straight out with virtually no algorithm intervention. Only when the night scene mode is on can you clearly feel the traces of HDR algorithm processing (although it doesn't spin around). I think Xiaomi's strategy is very bad. Blindly pursuing film production speed will only lead to making a lot of bad films. Very severe red overflow During use, I also discovered another problem: Xiaomi (which could also be a problem with Leica toning) has a noticeable overflow when shooting red, and the trigger rate is 100%, which is not an accident. This may be due to algorithm bias, as red was not specifically optimized. Having discussed the disadvantages, are there any advantages? The answer is definitely there. Since collaborating with Leica, Xiaomi has been praising its shades. Actually, I think Xiaomi's tone control is quite successful. Leica Classic, Leica Vibrant, and Leica Monochrome HC are sufficient to handle various scenes. Since I started using this phone, my friends have all called me a "landscape photography master". Leica monochrome HC filter, shooting location: Hechai 1972 And the main camera uses a variable aperture. Although there are only two settings, F/1.9 and F/4, F/4 is enough to prevent me from having blurry edges when shooting text. However, there is very little "variable aperture" involved in the photography process; most scenes are shot at F/1.9 (ps: This variable aperture alone makes many beginners mistakenly think the lens is cracked). Then there is the medium coke.There's not much to say about the medium focal length lens; it's the best 3x lens I've ever used, and the 75mm gold focal length takes great photos. However, it should be noted that the 3.2x lens of the Xiaomi 13 Ultra is actually cropped to 68mm (2.6x). If you want to use the entire lens, you need to manually pull it back to 68mm. The only drawback is that it doesn't provide a floating lens module (macro). I don't quite understand why the 13Pro is equipped with a telephoto macro lens, but the Ultra lens is simplified. Finally, the telephoto lensThe telephoto lens is a 5x 858 lens, with viewing parameters of 1/2.51 inches and an aperture of F3.0. In actual testing, the telephoto capability is actually similar to, or even inferior to, the IMX586 on the Xiaomi 10 Supreme Commemorative Edition, Xiaomi 11 Ultra, and Xiaomi 12 Sultra. After searching online, I discovered that the IMX858 is 2x2OCL, which is not naturally suitable for long-distance viewing, and its quality is definitely not as good as the IMX586. However, during use, I found that its color accuracy was better than that of its predecessor (12SUltra), which can be considered an improvement. In the May update, Xiaomi provided the 13Ultra with the same AI super telephoto lens as the 14Ultra via OTA, which is essentially using a large AI model to draw more details. In actual use, the telephoto ability has indeed been improved, but the effect is still not as good as the 14Ultra. My opinion is that it's good enough to have it, and it's already good enough that you can't remember to give it to me. Haven't you heard that outdated flagships and dogs are not allowed inside? portraitPortraits are arguably one of the worst parts of your life. What I want to say is that the rear camera is bad, not the front camera. Xiaomi's front-facing portrait algorithm is currently in the first tier and has gained recognition from many women around me. Previously, rear-facing portraits were always Leica-toned, focusing on making people look sallow, and the edge blurring was also poorly handled. At the end of May, with the update of the AI super telephoto lens, the latest Master Portrait was also released to the Xiaomi 13 Ultra. However, after comparison, I found that it was probably only a filter released to the 13 Ultra. The photography page still has a terrible lens package design (the default 75mm cannot switch lenses, and switching lenses requires using the soft focus, rotating focus, Portrait and other terrible effects in the lens package), so it can be said that there has been no improvement. The main camera interface doesn't have a switch button for the fast EV (it's really incredible that the Turbo3 gives you rice but doesn't upzoom), the professional mode isn't preset, and the continuous zoom for video recording is still being held back. In summary, it boils down to one sentence: outdated flagships are not as good as dogs. Besides, the 13Ultra isn't outdated at all. The official price was adjusted to 1400 on July 11th, and now you can buy the 12+256 for 3999. If you treat old machines like this, who will buy them in the future? Therefore, compared to the 14 Ultra, Turbo3, and Civi4 Pro, the Xiaomi 13 Ultra currently lacks professional mode shade preset, continuous video zoom, EV quick adjustment, and a new portrait UI (focal length adjustment). In fact, these are all software-level things. If there are strong developers, they can even port them over, but Mi just won't release them. This does not include things like 4K120, which may be hardware-related. As a developer user, spending most of my time on couplets for three consecutive months is really unbearable. III. Surrounding ConfigurationThere's not much to say about the peripheral configurations of Xiaomi's devices; they basically have everything you need, and none of them are too bad. For example, charging is 90W wired and 50W wireless, and a 5000mAh battery is basically standard (just to complain, why does your Mi 5000's battery have such poor battery life? It only lasts 4-5 hours on 4G). Infrared remote control, IP68, dual speakers, and USB 3.2 will also be included. Speaking of the screen, I personally think the quality of this C7 screen from CSOT is quite good, and the eye protection is quite good, but the power consumption is a bit high. I feel like I've never reached the advertised peak speed of 2600 nits; I still can't see the screen clearly outdoors.Just take a look at the advertisements for your rice. One downside of this phone is that it gets very hot easily, and the brightness drops when it gets hot. The abnormal body temperature is also not easy to dissipate, and it all accumulates on the index finger supporting the phone under the lens, which is not a good experience on hot days. Whether it's 4G/5G or WiFi signals, I think they can be considered top-tier, comparable to Huawei's. The Wi-Fi is quite fast, but downloads are frequently congested, causing my Huawei's internet speed to be very poor. systemXiaomi released its self-developed system, Xiaomi HyperOS, also known as Surge OS, along with the Xiaomi 14 last November. Before MIUI 12, many people said that Xiaomi's system had many bugs. I didn't believe it at the time and after getting Xiaomi, I found it to be really good. Xiaomi's operating system is currently the most convenient for me to use. Its small functions and UI design are very user-friendly and efficient. Speaking of bugs, I didn't encounter many. Maybe I'm not very sensitive to lag, but it was okay, except for the occasional slight frame drop. Adding your favorite features to MIUI and Surge after rooting will make it easier to use. Before I sold my Xiaomi 13 Ultra, it was the development version 1.0.24.7.8.DEV. Overall, compared to the first version, all the bugs have been fixed, the overall scheduling and overheating have also decreased a lot, and the system is generally smoother (of course, there is still a gap compared to the current T0). Never give up on a good phone just because you hear the system is bad. Everyone was hyping vivo's OriginOS 4, but after my recommendation, a friend bought the X100 Pro, and after experiencing it, I felt it was just so-so.Whether the system is good or not, you have to use it yourself to know.。 sum upOverall, the Xiaomi 13 Ultra is not a decent phone. Its distorted design, poor heat dissipation, and overheating provide a user experience that is inferior to its own Xiaomi 13, or even performance phones like the K60 and K70. However, his photography is indeed remarkable. Before the Xiaomi 14 Ultra came out, it was indeed the most well-rounded camera overall. There's a saying that goes: there's no such thing as an unsuitable machine, only an unsuitable price. Now the price of a used 13 Ultra has dropped below 3000, and you can buy a brand new 12+256 for 3999. If you have a limited budget but want to buy a phone with decent photography, the 13Ultra is definitely your best choice.

This round of policies will continue to affect Middle East shipping, oil supply, and international settlement risks. entry.title: Zhongyuan Festival: The Chinese July 15th Festival, from ancestor worship and Obon to Zhongyuan traditions | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. The fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month is called "Zhongyuan Festival" or "July and a Half" in many parts of China. If we only understand it as the "Ghost Festival", we will actually miss a more important aspect of this festival: it is related to the ancient traditions of autumn sacrifice and ancestor worship, and has also absorbed the Taoist concept of "Zhongyuan" and the Buddhist tradition of Obon. Later, rich customs such as ancestor worship, popularization, releasing river lanterns, and inviting family members have developed in different regions. The reason it has truly lasted for over a thousand years is not due to mysterious legends, but to how Chinese people face death, remember loved ones, maintain family relationships, and how they integrate "remembering the past" into the order of life throughout the year.
I. What is the Ghost Festival: Why is it celebrated on the 15th day of the seventh lunar month?The Zhongyuan Festival is usually held on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month, and in some areas on the fourteenth day of the seventh lunar month, so it is often directly referred to as "July and a half" by the people. July is the end of summer and the beginning of autumn. In traditional agricultural societies, a number of crops have already ripened. The ancients would pay homage to their ancestors with their new harvests, thank the land, and report the harvest to their ancestors. According to data from the China Intangible Cultural Heritage Network, the formation of the Zhongyuan Festival is closely related to ancient autumn sacrifices and ancestor worship. Later, it was gradually combined with the July 15th ceremony of Taoism and Buddhism, eventually forming the composite festival we see today.China Intangible Cultural Heritage Website Therefore, the Ghost Festival was not suddenly "invented" on a certain day, and it is difficult to explain it by a single religion. A more accurate understanding is that the original seasonal ancestor worship in agrarian society provided its social foundation, Taoism gave it the name "Zhongyuan" and the religious interpretation of local officials forgiving sins, and the Buddhist Obon tradition reinforced the theme of "repaying kindness to relatives and recommending the deceased" on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. These three traditions have intertwined over a long period of folk life, gradually forming the festival customs we are familiar with today. II. Where does the term "Zhongyuan" come from? The Taoist Trinity SystemThe name "Zhongyuan" itself comes from Taoism. Taoism refers to the fifteenth day of the first lunar month, the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month, and the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month as the Upper Yuan, the Middle Yuan, and the Lower Yuan, respectively, in accordance with the belief systems of Heavenly Officials, Earthly Officials, and Water Officials: the Upper Yuan is associated with Heavenly Officials bestowing blessings, the Middle Yuan is associated with Earthly Officials forgiving sins, and the Lower Yuan is associated with Water Officials relieving misfortune. The China Intangible Cultural Heritage Digital Museum's explanation of the Hong Kong Chao Ren Meng Lan Sheng Club also clearly refers to the 15th day of July as "Zhongyuan" in the Taoist sense.China Intangible Cultural Heritage Website - Chao Ren Meng Lan Sheng Hui In this system, Zhongyuan Day carries religious significance of examining good and evil, forgiving sins, and relieving misfortune. Later, Taoist priests held rituals such as fasting, chanting scriptures, and recommending the dead around the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month, and these practices gradually entered folk festival life. It should be noted that the Taoist "pardon of sins by local officials" belongs to the religious belief system and cannot be regarded as a verifiable historical fact; However, it did profoundly influence the way Chinese people understand the fifteenth of July and shaped later ritual language such as "popularizing" and "giving orphans". III. Obon and "Linking Eyes to Save Mother": Why Buddhism Also Values the July 15th FestivalAnother important tradition of the Ghost Festival comes from the Buddhist Ullambon festival. The Ullambhana Sutra tells the story of Vajrayana who wanted to save his deceased mother: He saw that his mother was suffering and could not be saved by his own strength, so the Buddha taught him to offer food to the monks on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month, the day when the monks were free, and to return the merit to his parents and relatives. The core of the scripture is not to create fear, but to emphasize repaying one's parents' kindness in raising them and expressing filial piety through the merits of spiritual practice in the monastic community.The Buddha's Discourse on the Obon Sutra After the Obon tradition was introduced to China, it resonated strongly with a social culture that already attached great importance to filial piety and ancestor worship. The story of "Mulian saving his mother" later spread widely through scripture lectures, literary changes, operas, and folk tales, gradually becoming one of the most influential stories of the July 15th festival. At the same time, the Chinese people did not abandon their original ancestor worship customs because of this, but instead combined the Buddhist concepts of recommending the dead and repaying kindness with family sacrifices. Therefore, it is inaccurate to simply say that the Ghost Festival "comes from Buddhism" or, conversely, to say that "Obon is just another name for the Ghost Festival". A more reasonable explanation is that the Buddhist Obon, the Taoist Zhongyuan, and the folk July ancestor worship initially had different ideological origins, but they influenced each other in China's long-term social practice, eventually forming overlapping festival cultures within the same period. IV. The True Core: Ancestor Worship, Remembrance, and "Remembering the Past"At the level of ordinary families, the most enduring core of the Ghost Festival is actually ancestor worship. In many places, seasonal fruits, meals, and drinks are prepared to offer sacrifices to ancestral tablets or cemeteries; Some places emphasize "inviting ancestors," "paying respects to ancestors," and "sending off ancestors," while other families only conduct simple memorial services. The Zhongyuan Festival custom in Laiwu, Shandong Province, is represented by "inviting family members," which combines ancestor worship with family reunion through stages such as "inviting, offering, worshipping, sending off, and gathering." This custom was later included in the national intangible cultural heritage representative project.Hubei Provincial Intangible Cultural Heritage Website From a cultural psychological perspective, the Zhongyuan Festival addresses a very simple question: after a person dies, how can the living continue to live with memories? Traditional societies transform longing into rituals that can be participated in together through fixed festivals. Preparing meals, arranging offerings, telling stories of ancestors, and having family gatherings may seem like everyday activities, but they allow family memories to be passed down from generation to generation. "Remembering the past" therefore explains why this festival has existed for so long better than "imagining ghosts and monsters". The so-called ancestor worship is not only an expression of sorrow, but also a way to confirm where one comes from, how one's family continues, and what responsibilities one should bear between people. The "filial piety" in the Ghost Festival is not only directed at deceased elders, but also reminds people in real life to cherish their loved ones who are still alive. V. Why Release River Lanterns: From Remembrance to Public MemoryReleasing river lanterns is one of the most visually symbolic customs of the Ghost Festival. Traditional river lanterns are mostly made in the shape of lotus flowers, lotus flowers, etc. After lighting the lanterns and candles, they are placed in rivers and lakes. Folk beliefs often attribute it to meanings such as "illuminating the underworld," "guiding the way," and "guiding the dead." From a socio-cultural perspective, it also transforms private remembrance into collective rituals in public spaces. The River Lantern Festival in Ziyuan County, Guangxi, is particularly representative. The area is located along the Zijiang River waterway. In the past, water transport was developed, but this also came with the risk of death for river engineers, sailors, and drainage workers. The local release of river lanterns during the Zhongyuan period not only serves as a tribute to ancestors but also as a way to mourn those who died on the water. The Ziyuhe Lantern Festival was listed as a national intangible cultural heritage representative project in 2014. Its materials clearly record a complete set of folk customs, including ancestor worship, lantern making, lantern release, and wishing making.China Intangible Cultural Heritage Network - Resources River Lantern Festival This shows that the same festival custom can carry completely different historical memories in different places. River lanterns can be part of a religious ceremony or a town's way of commemorating its waterway history, accident victims, and local community. Looking at river lanterns again today, it is more appropriate to understand them as a symbolic language for traditional society to process the memory of death, rather than treating the folk explanation of "illuminating the way for the dead" as a reality. VI. Pudu, Giving to Orphans, and Local Society: The Zhongyuan Festival is not just about honoring one's ancestors.The Zhongyuan Festival also has a very special characteristic: its recipients of care often expand from "original ancestors" to the unworshipped deceased. It is popularly known as "popularization" or "giving orphans away". The Hong Kong Chao Ren Meng Lan Sheng Club is a typical example. Local Holy Festival activities often include setting up altars to worship ancestors and offer prayers for the deceased, as well as community activities such as divine skill operas, peaceful rice, and lucky item competitions. It retains both Buddhist and Taoist rituals, while also bearing a strong sense of immigrant society and neighborhood community.China Intangible Cultural Heritage Website - Chao Ren Meng Lan Sheng Hui From a social function perspective, "sacrificing orphans" embodies a concept that expands from family ethics to public ethics: not only commemorating ancestors related to oneself by blood, but also taking care of those who have died who are symbolically "unsacrificed". When introducing the Zhongyuan Festival, Chinese intangible cultural heritage protection agencies summarize this tradition as a combination of commemorating ancestors, shedding light on the underworld to save orphans, and generosity.China Intangible Cultural Heritage Website Understanding these customs today does not require accepting all religious interpretations of them, but it allows us to see how traditional communities use festivals to build mutual aid, charity, public performances, and shared memories. VII. Why are they different from place to place: July 14th and July 15th and local festivalsChina has a vast territory, and there has never been a completely unified national custom for celebrating the Ghost Festival. In most places, the 15th of July is the center, while in some areas, the 14th of July is the main day of worship. Some places emphasize family sacrifices, some places emphasize grave sacrifices, some places emphasize river lanterns or sea lanterns, and some places form a popular celebration that lasts for many days. For example, in the past, the "July and a Half" festival in Guidong, Hunan Province, mainly involved family-by-family ancestor worship, which is different from the strong clan-based tomb sweeping during the Qingming Festival. An old custom along the coast of Weihai, Shandong, once included releasing sea lanterns to mourn those who died at sea. Guangxi's resources form a large-scale river lantern festival; Hong Kong's Teochew community has developed the Menglan Shenghui, which spans blocks. These differences demonstrate that the Ghost Festival is not a rigid "standard template," but rather a festival that various regions have continuously adapted according to their own production methods, geographical environment, clan structure, and religious traditions.Hunan Provincial People's Government Weihai Municipal People's Government The same applies to food. The Ghost Festival does not have a nationally unified seasonal food like Dragon Boat Festival zongzi and Mid-Autumn Festival mooncakes. Some places prepare duck, chicken, pastries, new rice, fruits, or home-style meals, but these are more local customs or sacrificial structures and cannot be simply said to mean that "the whole country eats a certain type of food during the Ghost Festival". When understanding traditional festivals, respecting these regional differences is more in line with historical reality than forcibly summarizing a "standard menu". 8. Is the "Ghost Festival" the true essence of the Ghost Festival?"Ghost Festival" is a common folk name for the Zhongyuan Festival, but it tends to overly mystify the festival. The sayings that "the gates of hell open" in the seventh lunar month, and that one should not go out at night, pat one's shoulder, or hang clothes to dry, are widely circulated in different places and in modern online culture. However, these are folk concepts, local taboos, or legends of later generations. They are not unified traditions that must be followed during the Ghost Festival, nor are they rules that have been verified by facts. Packaging the Ghost Festival only as "the most sinister day" obscures its most stable cultural structure: ancestor worship, repaying kindness, remembrance, giving alms to orphans, and family reunion. The so-called narratives of ghosts and spirits can be viewed as objects of folklore research, but fear should not be taken as the entire meaning of the festival. In fact, the summary of the Zhongyuan Festival in Chinese intangible cultural heritage materials emphasizes filial piety, ancestor worship, charity, community cohesion, and the inheritance of local culture, rather than a "complete list of taboos". If you want to introduce the Zhongyuan Festival to someone unfamiliar with Chinese culture, the best starting point is not to glorify the supernatural, but to explain how traditional Chinese society uses a fixed date to discuss life and death, kinship, memory, and ethics. 9. What are the differences between the Zhongyuan Festival and the Qingming Festival and the Cold Clothing Festival?These festivals are all related to ancestor worship, but the timing and ritual focus are not exactly the same. Qingming Festival falls in spring and is one of the twenty-four solar terms. Later, it incorporated traditions such as tomb sacrifice, cold food, and spring outings. Today, the most familiar Qingming Festival activities are sweeping tombs, laying flowers, tidying up cemeteries, and going on spring outings. Therefore, it emphasizes visiting cemeteries to commemorate the occasion in real space. During the late summer and early autumn, the Zhongyuan period, centered on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month, not only emphasized family ancestor worship but also traditions such as the Yulan basin, Pudu, orphan giving, and river lanterns. Therefore, the scope of worship objects and rituals was often wider than during the Qingming Festival. The Cold Clothing Festival usually falls around the first day of the tenth lunar month. After the cold season begins, the symbolic meaning of "giving away cold clothes" becomes more pronounced. There are records of old customs in Yantai, Shandong and other places such as visiting graves, burning paper towels and cutting winter clothes every October.Relevant local folk customs materials in Yantai City Together, the three constitute part of the Chinese ancestor worship culture at the age of 18, but it cannot be simply said which is "more authentic" or which completely replaces which. They are embedded in different seasonal nodes of spring, autumn, and winter, maintaining the commemorative relationship between the living and their ancestors in different ways. 10. How to celebrate the Ghost Festival today: Preserve remembrance and reduce risks.Modern society can still retain the cultural significance of the Ghost Festival, but the way it is expressed can change with lifestyle. Families can pay homage to their ancestors, organize old photos, tell family stories, prepare a familiar meal, or lay flowers at the cemetery. Communities and cultural institutions can also pass on traditions through river lantern displays, intangible cultural heritage activities, and local history explanations. At the same time, traditional practices such as burning incense, paper towels, and lighting open flames of river lanterns may lead to fires, air pollution, or garbage problems under conditions of urban environment, forest fire prevention, and water environmental protection. In recent years, many places have promoted methods such as flower-sweeping memorial services, online memorial services, and smokeless memorial services. Changing the medium does not mean cutting off tradition, because the core of sacrifice is not a specific object, but rather remembrance, gratitude, and commemoration itself. If we were to give the most appropriate explanation for the modern Ghost Festival, we could perhaps say that it is a day of the year dedicated to "remembering". People remember those who have passed away, they remember where they came from, and they remember that life is limited. Therefore, they should cherish the kinship and responsibility in reality even more. Conclusion: What did July 15th truly leave behind?The reason why the Ghost Festival is complex is precisely because it is not a single-line development tradition. Ancient autumn festivals and ancestor worship provided social fertile ground. Taoism gave it the name "Zhongyuan" and the belief in the three officials. The Buddhist tradition of the Obon reinforced the theme of repaying kindness to relatives and recommending the deceased. People in various places developed specific forms such as river lanterns, sea lanterns, universal lanterns, and invitations to family weddings according to their own living environments. If we summarize it with just the word "Ghost Festival," what we see is fear and taboo; If you broaden your horizons, you will find that it is really discussing a very universal human experience: how we face the departure of loved ones, how we preserve the memories of our families and local communities, and how we remind ourselves to cherish the present through rituals. This may be why the Ghost Festival is still worth introducing and understanding today. It does not require modern people to believe in the entire worldview of the ancients, but rather to show us how the Chinese people have expressed grief, filial piety, gratitude, and reverence for life throughout their long history.

Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. The English course name of ECON3116 is International Trade Theory and PolicyThat is, international trade theory and policy. This course doesn't just discuss "why countries exchange goods," but revolves around a complete economic theme: why different countries, industries, and companies form different trade patterns. How open trade can expand production and consumption possibilities; Why aren't trade gains automatically distributed equally domestically? And how prices, income distribution, and overall welfare change when governments use tariffs, quotas, subsidies, and trade agreements. After completely organizing the Lectures, tutorials, Quick quizzes, formula lists, and calculation problems, I understood the entire course as a four-layer interconnected framework: the first layer is...Source of tradeThis includes productivity differences, factor endowment differences, and economies of scale; The second layer isTrade resultsThis includes specialization, relative prices, income distribution, and welfare; The third layer isEnterprise and market structureExplain product differentiation, heterogeneous enterprises, exports, and FDI; The fourth layer isTrade Policy and SystemExplain protectionism, political incentives, the WTO, and preferential trade agreements.
I. Main Theme of the Course: Sources, Benefits, Distribution, and Policies of TradeInternational trade models each emphasize different sources of difference. The Ricardian model focuses on labor productivity; The Specific Factors model distinguishes between short-term industry-specific Factors and mobile labor; The Heckscher–Ohlin model explains relative factor endowment; Economies of scale and monopolistic competition illustrate that trade can occur even when countries are very similar; The heterogeneous enterprise model further explains why not all enterprises will export or become multinational corporations. The latter part of trade policy incorporates market outcomes into government decisions: whether tariffs can improve terms of trade, who receives quota rents, why protectionism persists politically, and when trade agreements create trade and when they divert it. When faced with new questions, I think the most useful thing is to ask four questions in sequence:
Who has a lower opportunity cost or unit cost? This determines comparative advantage, export direction, and business survival. Which relative price has changed? This determines production, consumption, factor rewards, and trade volume. Who was transferred, and who bore the distortion? This determines the welfare breakdown of tariffs, quotas, and subsidies. What are the key assumptions of the model? For example, can small countries influence world prices, whether factors of production flow, whether companies have market power, and who receives quota rent.
Explanatory questions can use a very stable English framework:
Define the model or concept → state the relevant price or cost change → explain the economic mechanism → identify the implication for trade, welfare, or income distribution.
That is:Define the model - locate the change - explain the mechanism - give the results。 II. Where does trade come from: Comparative advantages between Gravity Model and Ricardian1. Gravity Model: Let's look at the product relationship first.The Gravity Model illustrates that bilateral trade typically increases as the economies of both countries grow and decreases as geographical distance or trade frictions rise. Keeping all other conditions unchanged, the core relationship can be written as:
If both countries' GDPs double, trade volume will not double, but rather quadruple.
These types of questions test product relationships, not claims that real trade must increase exactly fourfold. The Gravity Model describes trade volume and partner distribution, while the Ricardian Model explains why a certain good is exported by a certain country; the two are not interchangeable. 2. Comparative advantage does not equal absolute advantageThe Ricardian model takes labor as the sole factor of production, and national differences arise from labor productivity or unit labor demand. Order the production of one unit of goods and The required labor is respectively 、Then one unit The opportunity cost is:

A country exports goods that have a lower opportunity cost. The key is not which country "produces more" of either commodity, but which gives up less of the other commodity in order to produce one more unit of the commodity. Absolute advantage influences living standards and wage levels, while comparative advantage determines the direction of specialization. If Home Below Foreign, the relative price of mutually beneficial trade needs to fall between the opportunity costs of self-sufficiency for both countries: $$\left(\frac{P_X}{P_Y}\right){Home}<\left(\frac{P_X}{P_Y}\right){trade}<\left(\frac{P_X}{P_Y}\right)_{Foreign}.$$ If the question is changed to "1 unit" How much can I exchange? "The relative price must be counted down, and the direction of the range must also be changed." The most common mistake here is to correctly calculate the opportunity cost but then use the wrong quotation direction as required by the question. III. Trade Gains Do Not Equal Benefits for Everyone: Specific Factors and H–O1. Specific Factors: Short-term industry distribution effectSpecific Factors, also known as the Ricardo–Viner model, typically have two departments. Labor can move across sectors, while capital or land is dedicated to specific industries. Under equilibrium competition, the wages of mobile workers satisfy:
If the relative price of manufactured goods As labor rises, it will flow from the food sector to manufacturing. Returns on dedicated capital in the manufacturing sector increased, while returns on dedicated land in the food sector decreased. Nominal wages for labor will rise, but are usually less than The increase, therefore:
Workers' actual wages, measured by different commodities, vary, making overall welfare uncertain. Special factors in the export sector are determined to benefit, while special factors in the import competition sector are determined to suffer. This difference from H–O is very important: Specific Factors is a short-term model with industry-specific elements; H–O is closer to a long-term adjustment, as both factors can be allocated across sectors, so the conclusion about the actual income of abundant and scarce factors is stronger. 2. Heckscher–Ohlin: Relative factor endowments shape tradeThe H–O model assumes that countries have the same technologies and preferences, but different relative factor endowments; Commodities are produced using different factor intensities. The abundance of factors is compared by the ratio of countries, for example ； The factor-intensive comparison is the input ratio in commodity production. The absolute amount of capital or the absolute labor force cannot determine "abundance" alone. The H–O theorem can be summarized as follows: a country exports goods that intensively use its relatively abundant factors, and imports goods that intensively use its relatively scarce factors. If Home is relatively labor-intensive and Cloth is relatively labor-intensive, Home will export Cloth and import capital-intensive goods. This module also has three closely related conclusions:
Stolper–Samuelson theoremAn increase in the relative price of a commodity will increase the real return of the commodity's intensively used factors, measured in terms of two commodities, and reduce the real return of the other factor. Rybczynski theoremWhen commodity prices remain constant, an increase in one factor will increase the output of goods that intensively use that factor, while the output of another will absolutely decrease. Factor Price EqualizationUnder strict conditions such as the same technology, the two countries producing the same goods, and very low trade costs, the convergence of commodity prices will lead to the convergence of actual returns on factors of production. Realistic technological differences, trade costs, and specialization can weaken this prediction.

IV. Standard Trade Model: Terms of Trade, Growth, and General EquilibriumThe standard trade model connects production and consumption using PPF, the no-difference curve, and the trade budget line. If domestic exports ,import The terms of trade are defined as:
Improved terms of trade mean that the same amount of exports can be exchanged for more imports, thus tending to improve domestic welfare. After opening up trade, production points may still be located on the PPF, while consumption points may be outside the country's PPF. Exports and imports are not equal in physical quantity, but in value:
Growth does not necessarily improve welfare unconditionally. If growth is clearly biased towards exports, the relative global supply will increase, and the relative price tendency of exports will decrease:
Therefore, export-biased growth usually worsens domestic terms of trade. In extreme cases, relative price losses may even offset the expansion of production capacity; this is the logic of impoverished growth. When answering the questions, you should analyze "PPF outward expansion" and "changes in international relative prices" separately. V. Economies of Scale and Imperfect Competition: Similar Countries Also Trade1. Internal economies of scale and linear demandIf the total cost of the enterprise is:

Trade gains here come from economies of scale, increased variety, and increased competition, rather than just traditional comparative advantage. 2. Constant elasticity requirements: Do not mix with linear models.The Tutorial also uses constant elastic requirements:
It is the absolute value of the price elasticity of demand. The profit maximization condition is , thus:
The larger the markup, the more price-sensitive the consumer is; the smaller the markup, the closer the price is to marginal cost. Fixed costs will enter the zero-profit condition and the size of the enterprise, but they do not directly determine this markup formula. Here we need to distinguish between three sets of environments: perfect competition is... ； The optimal conditions for both monopolistic enterprises and monopolistic competitors are ； Linear demand and constant elastic demand will introduce different pricing formulas. We cannot mix all the formulas together just because we see the words "monopolistic competition". VI. Enterprise Heterogeneity, Exports, and FDIThe heterogeneous enterprise model classifies enterprises in an industry according to marginal cost. Arrangement. If the threshold for survival in the domestic market is Exports also incur unit trade costs. Export conditions are stricter:

Therefore, exporters are the lower-cost, more productive subset of surviving enterprises. Trade opening enables low-cost enterprises to expand and export, while high-cost enterprises contract or exit, and average industry productivity increases due to resource reallocation. Horizontal FDI is when companies replicate their production processes overseas to reach consumers; its core is... proximity–concentration trade-offWhen trade costs are high, proximity to the market is more attractive; When economies of scale are strong and overseas factories have high fixed costs, exports after concentrated production are more attractive. If overseas sales are Unit trading cost is The fixed cost of building a factory is The simplified comparison is:
Vertical FDI, on the other hand, moves part of the value chain to countries with lower production costs, primarily driven by wages, input costs, and comparative advantages. A company's ownership of an overseas institution falls under the category of offshoring/FDI; Entrusting production to an independent foreign company is considered foreign outsourcing. Exports versus FDI numerical frameworkIf foreign market demand is The marginal cost of local production is 20%, the fixed cost of FDI is 79%, and the export transportation cost is... Generally, counter-demand The marginal return is:

It is impossible to directly compare after fixing any arbitrary output. with Because transportation costs themselves change the optimal price and sales volume at the time of export. VII. Trade Policy: Set prices first, then calculate quantity and benefits.1. Tariffs between small and large countriesHome's import demand and Foreign's export supply are:
$$XS(P^)=S^(P^)-D^(P^*).$$ Free trade equilibrium satisfaction 。 Small countries cannot influence world prices and impose specific tariffs After:
Domestic supply increased, demand decreased, and imports decreased. Consumer surplus declined, producer surplus increased, and the government obtained... Tariff revenue, of which It must be the import volume after taxation. Net welfare losses consist of production and consumption distortions:
Small countries have no terms-of-trade benefits, so net welfare is bound to decline. Major countries must differentiate between tariffs paid by their own consumers. Received from foreign exporters ：
If 、 、 Simultaneously obtained The trade volume was 10. Cannot substitution , also cannot substitution 。 The welfare changes of major country tariffs are:
It may be positive, but it does not mean that a trade war is beneficial: trading partners may retaliate, and the optimal tariff conclusion is highly dependent on the country's actual market power. 2. Quotas, export subsidies and dumpingImport quotas are binding only if they are below the free trade import volume:
The post-quota price is determined by the following formula:
Equivalent tariffs and quota rents are:
Quotas and equivalent tariffs can produce the same prices, quantities, and distortions, but the benefits depend on rent vesting. When a government auction license or domestic license holder receives rent, the domestic benefit may be the same as the equivalent tariff; If a foreign exporter obtains a license or receives rent under the VER, the country will lose this portion of its revenue. Export subsidies raise domestic prices and production, harm consumers, and incur government expenses; Major powers will also experience deteriorating terms of trade due to falling world export prices. Dumping relies on imperfect competition and market segmentation, with companies' net landed prices in export markets being lower than their domestic prices. Anti-dumping duties may also become protectionist tools in practice. VIII. Political Economy, WTO and Preferential Trade AgreementsThe net loss of tariffs in small countries is still widespread, and the reason cannot be explained by efficiency models alone. The protection benefits of importing competing producers are highly concentrated, while the losses of consumers are dispersed among many people. Therefore, the former has more incentive to organize lobbying:
Import-competing producers are more likely to lobby for protection because their gains are concentrated, whereas consumers’ losses are dispersed.
The Protection for Sale model further integrates campaign contributions and social welfare into government objectives, predicting that organized industries are more likely to be protected. It does not assume that the government is completely indifferent to social welfare, but rather gives extra weight to organized interests. The WTO and multilateral negotiations reduce retaliatory trade wars by lowering tariffs, constraining future tariff increases, addressing non-tariff barriers, and providing dispute settlement mechanisms. Countries may prefer protection when acting alone, but protecting each other can make both sides worse off than common free trade, and enforceable agreements can alleviate this prisoner's dilemma. The benefits of preferential trade agreements should be distinguished:
Trade creationReal resource costs have decreased due to a shift from higher-cost domestic production to lower-cost imports from member countries. Trade diversionShifting from the lowest-cost non-member country to a member country that appears cheaper due to zero tariffs but has higher actual costs may result in a decline in benefits.
For example, non-member C has a cost of 4 and member B has a cost of 6. Before the agreement, both bear a tariff of 3, and the country imports from C, which has a CIF price of 7. After the agreement, only B was exempted from taxes, and the source of imports was changed to B at a price of 6. Consumers pay 1 less per unit, but the government loses the original 3 tariff per unit; the net change is... 。 When determining the PTA, it is essential to compare the pre- and post-agreement periods.True source of production costsIt's not just the price that consumers see. IX. The most effective methods and typical mistakes in reviewThe most effective way to organize this course is not to reread the PPT continuously, but to compress each model into a small loop of "recognizing words - core equations - directional conclusions - a similar problem". For example, the H–O numerical problem first uses the full employment equation to calculate output, and then uses the zero profit equation to calculate... ； For FDI questions, first write trade costs into marginal costs, and then maximize profits separately; The tariff question uses a fixed five-step order of "price-quantity table-consumer surplus and producer surplus-government revenue-net welfare". Several typical errors occurred during the review process:
The proportional relationship only changes onceThe simultaneous doubling of the GDP of both countries was mistakenly interpreted as a doubling of trade; instead, the product was used to expand the result to four times. H–O equation algebraic errorThe conditions for full employment are written correctly, but the result after elimination is incorrect; The answer can only be confirmed after subtracting item by item and returning the resource constraint. put Used for monopolistic enterprises: should be changed to And distinguish between perfect competition, linear monopoly and constant elastic monopoly competition. Exports and FDI were not optimized separately.Transportation costs change the optimal price and sales volume for exports, so maximized profits must be compared. Major powers only seek one price for tariffs.: Must use Integrate import demand and export supply. Quota rents are confused with government revenueFirst, indicate the ownership of the license, and then determine the welfare of the country.
These errors can be further divided into four categories: concept recognition, equation setting, algebraic calculation, and economic interpretation. You don't need to reread the entire chapter each time you get a wrong question; simply identify the error category and complete a similar question immediately. For graphics questions, you should also mark them first. The pre-tax and post-tax quantities and each welfare area are then used to calculate the area. After completing the numerical questions, perform at least two backtests. First, the substitution equation: H–O production must be exactly used up. Monopolistic enterprises Demand must be met again. Second, examine the economic direction: tariffs should reduce imports, rising transportation costs should reduce export sales, increased labor should expand the output of labor-intensive goods, and export growth should suppress the relative prices of exports. When the results are opposite to these directions, priority should be given to checking the symbols, price variables, and whether after-tax quantities were used. 10. In the exam room, the multiple-choice questions should first identify "short-term Specific Factors or long-term H-O", "small country or large country", "linear demand or constantly elastic demand", and "who should receive the quota rent". For calculation problems, first define variables, write equations, substitute numbers, and finally explain the economic meaning in one sentence. The choice of model often determines the answer more than the arithmetic itself. XI. Conclusion: Treating trade theory as an analytical languageThe most worthwhile takeaway from ECON3116 is not memorizing a single tariff area formula, but a transferable analytical sequence: first look for cost or endowment differences, then observe how relative prices are transmitted to production, consumption, and factor returns, and finally distinguish between real efficiency changes, income transfers, and unnecessary losses. Comparative advantage explains why trade can be mutually beneficial; Specific Factors and H–O explain who will support or oppose trade; Economies of scale, heterogeneous firms, and FDI describe firm-level adjustments; Trade policy and political economy remind us that efficiency conclusions do not automatically translate into policy choices. Only by placing formulas under model assumptions, graphs after price changes, and welfare judgments within the decomposition of transfer and distortion can we stably reconstruct answers in unfamiliar situations, rather than relying solely on memory for a particular question.
